title.narrative: The Chaco Jaguar Conservation Project: Establishing a Participatory Stakeholder.Conflict Reduction Program to Effect Long-Term, Broad-scale Jaguar Conservation and Connectivity in Paraguay

description.narrative: The purpose of this project is to secure the long-term future of jaguar populations in five geographical regions of the Paraguayan Gran Chaco by reducing mortality on private land, promoting coexistence between humans and jaguars, and connecting jaguar habitat and populations through the cooperation and participation of landowners. Project objectives include (i) establishing an effective conflict mitigation program based on a functional, participatory network of approximately 20 livestock producers willing to suspend killing predators and explore alternative scenarios for reducing conflict; (ii) collecting data on human-predator conflict mitigation for broad-scale analysis to inform the development of new policy and livestock management and husbandry guidelines; (iii) developing custom management and mitigation strategies for landowners, including an economic appraisal of option trade-offs; and (iv) promoting the conflict reduction program among the public, conservation professionals, and individual and commercial livestock producers.

person-name.narrative: William Jones; Colleen Holland; Julie Rice; Ry
